bottom_line: In patients undergoing PCI, double-dose clopidogrel reduced cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke at 30 days versus standard-dose clopidogrel (adjusted hazard ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.74–0.99).
implications: These 30-day PCI-subgroup results support that double-dose clopidogrel (vs standard-dose) was associated with a lower rate of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke (3.9% vs 4.5%; adjusted HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.74–0.99) and lower definite stent thrombosis (0.7% vs 1.3%; HR 0.54, 0.39–0.74), while increasing CURRENT-defined major bleeding (1.6% vs 1.1%; HR 1.41, 1.09–1.83). In the same PCI population, the trial does not show a difference between high-dose and low-dose aspirin for the primary outcome (4.1% vs 4.2%; HR 0.98, 0.84–1.13).

major_points.text: Clopidogrel dose comparison was double-blind; aspirin comparison was open label with blinded outcome adjudication.
major_points.quote: The clopidogrel dose comparison was double-blind and the aspirin dose comparison was open label with blinded assessment of outcomes.

major_points.text: Primary outcome was cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke at 30 days.
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke at 30 days.

major_points.text: Double-dose clopidogrel reduced the primary outcome versus standard-dose clopidogrel.
major_points.quote: Compared with the standard dose, double-dose clopidogrel reduced the rate of the primary outcome (330 events [3·9%] vs 392 events [4·5%]; adjusted hazard ratio 0·86, 95% CI 0·74–0·99, p=0·039)

major_points.text: Major bleeding was more common with double-dose than standard-dose clopidogrel.
major_points.quote: Major bleeding was more common with double-dose than with standard-dose clopidogrel (139 [1·6%] vs 99 [1·1%]; 1·41, 1·09–1·83, p=0·009)

major_points.text: High-dose and low-dose aspirin did not differ for the primary outcome.
major_points.quote: High-dose and low-dose aspirin did not diﬀer for the primary outcome (356 [4·1%] vs 366 [4·2%]; 0·98, 0·84–1·13, p=0·76).
